chunks.arabic_text: عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنِ أَيُّوبَ، الْقُمِّيُّ. ذَكَرَهُ الْغُلَاةُ، وَرَوَوْا عَنْهُ. لَا نَعْرِفُهُ.

translations.en: ʿAbdullāh b. Ayyūb, al-Qummī. The ghulāt mentioned him and narrated from him. He is not recognized.

en.summary: This entry highlights ʿAbdullāh ibn Ayyūb al-Qummī as a transitional figure whose authority was contested due to his association with the Ghulāt (Exaggerators), a group known for theological innovations such as divine incarnation. While the Ghulāt utilized his narrations to support their specific doctrines, mainstream scholars remained skeptical of his reliability, illustrating the critical process of biographical evaluation (ʿilm al-rijāl) used to distinguish authentic transmission from sectarian appropriation.
en.seo_question: Who is ʿAbdullā ibn Ayyūb al-Qummī and what is his status in Shia hadith sciences?

key_terms.الغلاة: Ghulāt (Exaggerators), a group known for attributing divine qualities to Imams or holding extreme views.
key_terms.لا نعرفه: La naʿrifuhu (He is not known/recognized), indicating a narrator whose reliability or identity is uncertain or weak.
